newsitem.title: GERMANY: Spain's Rato says not worried by peseta rise.
newsitem.headline: Spain's Rato says not worried by peseta rise.

text.p: Spanish Economy Minister Rodrigo Rato said on Wednesday he was not concerned by recent strength in the peseta against the German mark.
Speaking in Bonn, he said: "It's been moving between 84-something and 83-something (to the mark) during the past month. It's a decision by markets...we are not worried about it."
The peseta has been strong recently, but has fallen back this week following comments by Spanish politicians indicating they believed the exchange rate was too high.

German Finance Ministry number two Juergen Stark knocked back the Spanish unit on Tuesday by saying that some countries that would qualify on paper for European monetary union may not be structurally ready.

The peseta stood at 84.61/63 to the mark in late trading on Wednesday. Market traders said they believed that the Bank of Spain had bought small amounts of pesetas to shore up the national currency against the mark.
Rato added: "The Spanish peseta has been moving in a range that is predictable, neither too low nor too high. It's been staying in the same range for a long period of time.
"The Spanish peseta is a stable currency, and it's going to stay that way."
